sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Physical Scarcity vs. Economic Scarcity**: Physical scarcity occurs when water resource development exceeds sustainable limits (e.g., Northwest India), whereas economic scarcity arises from a lack of investment in infrastructure or institutional capacity (e.g., parts of Sub-Saharan Africa and Eastern India).
• **Cubic Metre Per Capita Benchmark**: According to Falkenmark Indicator, a country experiences water stress when annual water supplies drop below **1,700 cubic metres** per person, and absolute water scarcity below **1,000 cubic metres**.
• **Blue Water vs. Green Water**: Blue water represents liquid freshwater in rivers, lakes, and aquifers; green water represents soil moisture derived from precipitation that is absorbed by vegetation.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: India supports nearly **18% of the world's population** but has only **4% of the world's water resources**, making per capita water availability critically low and declining.

items.term: Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain
items.definition: National campaign launched with the theme 'Catch the rain, where it falls, when it falls' to nudge stakeholders to create rainwater harvesting structures.
Mission aimed at developing and rejuvenating 75 water bodies in each district of the country as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav to augment rural water security.

Formulated by the Ministry of Water Resources to govern the planning, development, and optimum utilization of water resources with a declared priority order (Drinking water, irrigation, hydro-power, ecology, agro-industries).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Over-exploited Groundwater Belts**: Northwest India (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP), parts of Southern peninsular India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) due to intensive paddy and wheat cultivation powered by free/subsidized electricity.
• **Traditional Water Conservation Regions**: Rajasthan (Tankas, Johads, Jhalaras), Maharashtra (Phad system), Western Himalayas (Kuls), and Meghalaya (Bamboo drip irrigation).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Fragmented institutional governance, heavy electricity subsidies promoting wasteful extraction, water pollution from untreated industrial effluents, and lack of community ownership.
• **Policy Interventions**: Shift from flood irrigation to micro-irrigation, conjunctive use of surface and groundwater, treating wastewater for industrial reuse, and empowering river basin organizations.

items.title: Mnemonic for National Water Policy Priority Order
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **D**rinking **I**rrigation **H**ydropower **E**cology **I**ndustry (DIHEI)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Drinking water > Irrigation > Hydro-power > Ecology > Industries & Navigation.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly answers questions regarding the hierarchical allocation of water resources during scarcity.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember the '3 R's of Water Conservation' for Mains introduction: **Reduce** (consumption), **Reuse** (greywater), and **Recycle** (sewage treatment plants).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that 'Water is a Union List subject under the Indian Constitution.' This is INCORRECT. Water is primarily in the State List (Entry 17), with the Union having powers only regarding inter-state rivers under Article 262.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the NITI Aayog Composite Water Management Index (CWMI) and Mihir Shah Committee recommendations on restructuring water governance (forming a National Water Commission) to fetch extra marks.

keyTakeaways: India faces severe structural water stress driven by agricultural over-extraction in the Northwest and institutional deficits.
Effective conservation requires shifting from supply-side engineering projects to demand-side management and watershed-level decentralization.
Constitutional provisions place water in the State List, necessitating cooperative federalism via bodies like Jal Shakti Ministry and inter-state tribunals.
